why_relevant: Largest non-chain SK research agency, ESOMAR/SAVA member; runs consumer and e-commerce studies whose toplines are released publicly and that occasionally cover payment method choice at checkout.

source_name: SAVA — Slovenská asociácia výskumných agentúr (member directory)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of SK market-research vendors; the cleanest way to enumerate every agency that could be commissioned for payment-behaviour or cash-usage studies, including small local players invisible to English search.
Leading SK opinion-research house; commissioned omnibus waves are a common vehicle for financial-behaviour questions (cash preference, trust in banks), released via clients rather than the agency.

source_name: Inštitút finančnej politiky (IFP) — MF SR analytical unit publications
why_relevant: Government-embedded think tank publishing komentáre/analýzy that re-cut banking-sector data (bank levy, sector profitability, credit); local-language register distinct from NBS statistics, and often uses microdata not otherwise published.
Single index of all SK ministerial analytical units' outputs; lets one query surface finance/banking analyses across IFP and sister institutes without crawling each ministry.

source_name: INESS — Inštitút ekonomických a spoločenských analýz
why_relevant: Independent SK economic think tank that comments on bank taxation, monetary policy and cash/digital-euro debates; provides the non-official analytical voice and often republishes sector figures in accessible form.

source_name: Sektorová rada pre bankovníctvo, finančné služby, poisťovníctvo — sector analysis (Národná sústava povolaní)
why_relevant: Tripartite sector council publishing a structured SK banking/payments sector analysis (SWOT, structural trends on instant payments, open banking, digital euro, branch reduction) — an unusual analytical channel most scans miss.

source_name: NBS Working Papers / Policy Briefs — payment behaviour and cash research (academic register)
why_relevant: Central-bank research arm functions as an analytical intermediary: household transaction-data studies of cash in circulation and digital-euro user surveys for SK, indexed also on RePEc.

source_name: Academic paper: Trends in the Development of the Payment Services Market — A case of Slovakia (Bobenič Hintošová et al.)
why_relevant: Concrete example of SK university research on the payment-services market; demonstrates that EUBA/UPJŠ-affiliated academics publish quantified SK payment analyses in open conference proceedings and on ResearchGate.

source_name: FinStat.sk — company financials of SK research/consulting firms and payment intermediaries
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: filed accounts of research agencies, acquirers and payment intermediaries give revenue trajectories that proxy market activity and confirm which actors are real and active.

Independent Slovak finance/business news portal with dense, recurring coverage of payments: mandatory cashless acceptance from March 2026, merchant terminal counts (e.g. '117 000 podnikateľov'), Revolut launching payment terminals for Slovak merchants. Frequently sources figures directly from banks/acquirers rather than from NBS releases.

Specialised Slovak banking/insurance/fintech trade portal with dedicated FinTech and 'Banky a poisťovne' rubrics. Publishes explainer/comparison pieces built on bank-by-bank answers (contactless ATM withdrawal availability per bank, cash withdrawal abroad fees), i.e. exactly the vendor-relevant detail absent from NBS aggregates.

Consumer banking comparison/editorial portal that maintains recurring, explicitly data-driven explainer pages on exactly this cell's metrics: 'Počet platobných kariet a bankomatov na Slovensku', 'Koľko je na Slovensku vydaných platobných kariet', card-transaction growth over 10 years. Acts both as a direct figure source and as a pointer to the NBS/SBA datasets it cites.

Slovak IT/technology magazine that covers ATM hardware modernisation, NFC/cardless withdrawal, self-service banking and mobile payments — the IT-trade angle of this cell. Its brandit.touchit.sk press-release arm republishes vendor and scheme releases (e.g. Mastercard mobile-payment penetration in Slovakia), which is a fast channel for scheme/vendor survey numbers.

Private Slovak news agency's finance desk; primary originator of many payment stories that other outlets republish (e.g. QR-payment volumes exceeding EUR 10m). Agency copy is the earliest timestamp for bank/ministry-supplied figures and therefore the best signal-detection layer.

State news agency TASR's public portal; economy desk carries NBS/SBA/ministry payment announcements and legislative news on the cashless-acceptance obligation. High-volume, well-timestamped, and widely mirrored by regional media.

Business section of one of Slovakia's largest dailies. Runs bank-fee investigations and reader-driven stories (e.g. mBank fee increases, ATM withdrawal charges) and routinely polls banks directly for branch/ATM counts. Its reader discussion threads also surface early complaints about fee/ATM changes.

English-language Slovak outlet (SME group) that summarises TASR/NBS payment and card statistics for foreign readers — e.g. debit-card transaction and ATM/POS network volumes. Useful bridge for non-Slovak-speaking analysts and for cross-checking translations of local figures.

Long-running Slovak personal-finance portal with a dedicated 'Banky' rubric; republishes agency and bank press material on fees, ATM networks and card usage, and maintains bank product/fee reference pages. High-frequency, low-friction access.

High-traffic Slovak general-interest news site whose money desk produced a data-led piece on the shrinking Slovak ATM estate ('Bankomaty na Slovensku pomaly miznú') including a bank planning to add ~50 machines — the kind of bank-supplied, quarter-specific device counts that never appear in official releases.

Popular Slovak news/lifestyle site that covers branch and ATM closures bank by bank (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa branch/ATM cuts). Low analytical value but a fast tripwire for cash-access shrinkage events at named institutions.

Consumer-finance portal publishing recurring bank rankings and current-account/fee comparisons ('Najlepšie bežné účty 2026'), which encode per-bank ATM-withdrawal fee structures and cash-access terms — a usable proxy series for fee-driven cash behaviour.

Broker-run reference listing of banks operating in Slovakia — a compact actor map for snowballing into each institution's press room, branch/ATM locator and fee schedule. Pointer value, not statistical value.

Free, structured actor map of Slovak banks and branches of foreign banks with official names and links — useful for building the entity/alias list media coverage must be matched against (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa / SLSP, Tatra banka, VÚB, ČSOB, 365.bank, Prima banka, Fio, mBank, UniCredit).

Regional Slovak news site that published a bank-by-bank comparison of ATM cash-withdrawal limits and fees (UniCredit 40 banknotes, Prima banka EUR 300, Fio EUR 8 000, mBank EUR 70 threshold). Regional outlets are also the first to report local branch/ATM removals in smaller towns — the granular cash-access shrinkage signal.

Aggregating Slovak news portal that republishes payment-statistics releases (e.g. QR-payment transaction counts and value milestones). Useful as a redundancy layer to catch releases missed on primary desks.

Slovak news portal covering state assessment of the QR-payment rollout and record volumes; captures the political/fiscal framing of cashless adoption (state as promoter of QR payments) that shapes merchant acceptance policy.

Subscription-funded Slovak daily with a strong economics desk and a live economy feed; covers banking levy, bank fee changes and payment legislation with original reporting and direct bank questioning. Independent editorial stance makes it a credible counterweight to PR-driven portals.

source_name: SBA - Slovenská banková asociácia, card issuing/acquiring statistics newsroom
why_relevant: Not media itself, but the recurring dataset ('Štatistika vydávania a prijímania platobných kariet', monthly/quarterly) that Slovak trade media quote as their base for card and terminal counts. Essential for de-duplicating and validating media-reported figures in this cell; also identifies which outlets pick it up first.
